result:
All 31 tests pass. No bugs were found in `CSVParser` during this pass — every test failure I hit along the way turned out to be an incorrect assumption in my test (e.g. `CSVFormat.DEFAULT` has no header by default, `DuplicateHeaderMode.ALLOW_ALL` is the default, missing-but-allowed header names are still added to the header list, and `getRecords()`/`stream()` wrap `CSVException` in `UncheckedIOException` while package-private `nextRecord()` throws it directly) — not an actual defect in the code, so I corrected the tests rather than leaving them failing.

I created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVParserAgentTest.java` with 31 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering: all static `parse` factory methods (String/File/Path, including null-argument checks), header map/name handling (explicit headers, headers read from the first line, skip vs. no-skip, missing/blank column names, duplicate detection both at `CSVFormat` build time and at `CSVParser` runtime for dynamically-read headers), null-string handling, trailing-delimiter semantics (including the quoted-empty-field exception), header/trailer comments, iterator contract (`hasNext`/`next`/`remove`, behavior after `close()`), record numbering with offsets (deprecated constructor and builder), `maxRows`, `getRecordNumber`/`getCurrentLineNumber`, `isClosed`/idempotent `close`, and an invalid-input case asserting `CSVException`.
